title: StokEngineer — Stokastic Reverse Engineering
description: Zero-network, dependency-free DFS projection and optimizer rebuild of Stokastic's public methodology, self-contained and re-runnable offline, that separates official sources (DraftKings scoring rules, FanDuel, MLB Stats API, nflverse, NBA stats endpoints), reverse-engineered vendor methodology and independent analysis, and ships its own multi-sport projection engine: src/projection_engine/ holds 8 modules — data_sources, nba_projections, nfl_projections, mlb_projections, ownership_model, boom_bust, top_stacks and simulation_engine — with a deterministic optimizer that adds a stack constraint, ownership leverage, diversity, exposure and what-if lineups to the base knobs. The project's honest boundary is explicit: Stokastic's exact projection weights, sigma model and ownership coefficients are not public, so nothing claims them. VERIFICATION.md at commit 7dedfea is an 89-line document describing the mechanism rather than the 24-line claim log it was at the previous read, and the machine-readable claim log now lives in src/data/claims.json, which holds 25 claims (19 verified, 5 flagged, 1 not_verified). src/data/sources_verified.json is the machine-readable source registry: 29 sources (13 fetched_live in session, 5 github_api, 11 carried_over and explicitly treated as unverified) plus 4 removed_or_downgraded, and src/stokengineer/provenance.py refuses to use a source id that is not in it while tools/check_links.py re-walks every URL. IRREGULARITY: the repository's own test suite fails at this head — `PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m pytest tests -rA` gives 84 passed, 3 skipped and 1 FAILED (tests/test_optimizer.py::test_stack_constraint_produces_a_qb_stack, which raises _BudgetedOut: no legal lineup exists under these constraints), while `python -m src.stokengineer.cli verify` still reports OK (IRR-100). The previous version of this entry published '38 source entries across six categories', '155 verified badges' and 'a 24-line claim log'; none of those figures, nor the 71,004-byte site or the 7 flagged irregularities it also cited, is re-derivable from the current tree.

The repository caught a false claim about itself and recorded it. PASSES.md's Session 2 states that the demo returned roughly 21,000 percent Sim ROI and that PASSES.md had claimed this was fixed when it was not; the root cause was field lineups generated from a player pool the same size as the roster, so every 'field' lineup was a permutation of all players and tied the user lineup. Field generation was rewritten so the pool exceeds the roster, an illustrative GPP payout curve with documented rake was added, a guard now raises when pool size equals lineup size, and the ad-hoc covariance was replaced with a PSD projection.

An earlier README claimed '40+ verified sources' for a registry that held 38 entries. Commit 1842144 ('fix: re-verify all sources live; fix ROI-understated bug, pricing labels, dead links') removed the numeric claim and re-verified the registry, which at this head also carries 7 irregularities instead of 4 — including four source URLs from earlier builds that now redirect to a homepage, and DraftKings how-to-play and DK Network scoring pages that moved or 404. The counted 38 is what this entry publishes.

Everything proprietary is labelled inference rather than reproduced: exact projection weights are not published and the engine uses minutes 40 percent, usage 25 percent, matchup 20 percent, recent form 10 percent and other 5 percent; historical ownership is private and proxied with optimal percent plus salary; the correlation matrix is a heuristic (0.6 QB-WR, 0.3 WR-WR) rather than a measured joint distribution; the demo simulator's contest payout curve is illustrative; and the pricing page is coupon-gated and seasonally dynamic, so both toggles were recorded on 2026-09-22 with a note that a manual reviewer should re-fetch it live.

There is no test suite. The repository ships tools/check_links.py, which resolves every cited URL and exits 1 on a definitively dead link (treating 403/405/406/429/418 as bot-blocked but alive), but no unit tests, so the 24-line log is documentation-level evidence.
